patients.label: 27-year-old man with subhepatic acute appendicitis treated by appendectomy

identity_evidence.quote: A 27-year-old Black Ethiopian male from a rural part of the Oromia region

attribution_limitations: Source conflict on the stool examination: the abstract says it revealed many pus and red blood cells and actively motile bacteria, while Table 1 lists the stool examination as few pus cells.

The abstract says laboratory investigations were unremarkable apart from the stool examinations, but the text and Table 1 give increased erythrocyte sedimentation rate and procalcitonin, and Table 1 prints several other values outside the printed reference intervals.
The abstract calls subhepatic acute appendicitis an assessment that was suspected before the emergency operation, while the Case presentation states it as the diagnosis made before surgery.

Figure 1 panel B caption gives an appendix diameter of 6.55 mm and a fecalith depth of 1 cm identical to the ultrasound values, so it is not stated whether these describe the ultrasound image or the removed specimen.
The sentence on the ultrasound findings does not make clear whether the appendix or the fecalith was partially compressible.

The Discussion states that an ultrasound scan revealed a tubular hypoechoic formation at the area of greatest tenderness without a literal link to this patient or to the ultrasound in the Case presentation.
Table 1 prints the hemoglobin unit as mg/dl, the creatinine reference range as 0-5—1.2 and the calcium value as 9.401.

The Patient perspective text describes agonizing right upper abdominal pain, nausea and a low fever for the past five days and mild pain at the wound site, while the case text describes periumbilical pain that later radiated and a clean surgical wound at follow-up; the nausea is not mentioned elsewhere.

The Case presentation text gives an erythrocyte sedimentation rate of 32 mm/hr and a procalcitonin of 1.51 ng/mL, the same values as the Table 1 day-of-admission rows, but neither cites Table 1 nor states a time, so it is not stated whether these are the same measurements.

The Introduction says a chronic course with ill-defined right flank and right upper quadrant pain was the case in this report, while the Case presentation describes a 5-day history of periumbilical pain radiating to the right upper abdomen.

evidence.quote: (A) the yellow arrow shows the level of surgical incision at the level of the umbilicus while the pink arrow shows the removed appendiceal tissue with signs of inflammation.
(B) An inflamed appendix measuring 6.55mm in diameter (yellow arrow) with an internal fecalith 1 cm in depth (pink arrow), suggestive of acute appendicitis.
